title.narrative: Provision of essential lifesaving primary health services to vulnerable communities in under-served and hard-to-reach areas to reduce morbidity and morbidity in Baletweyne Districts, Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project will be carried out in Beledweyne district, in Hiraan region, to address the healthcare needs of vulnerable communities affected by climatic shocks such as droughts and floods, as well conflicts. The project is in response to Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) 1st standard allocation for 2025. It aligns with the strategic objective of implementing multisectoral responses in priority districts based on the HNRP 2025, to uphold ongoing efforts to prevent the worsening of needs and mitigate further displacement.ltbrgtIn line with this, the project aims to deliver the 6 CORE EPHS package services through 2 statics (1 health centers and 1 PHU) and 1 Mobile outreach service to the affected communities living in hard-to-reach areas in Baletweyne. The project will serve 4 IDPs camp with a population of six thousand. Service to be provided will include including maternal, reproductive neonatal health, communicable diseases control, child health and first aid. Approximately 43,000 individuals will benefit from this intervention, including 32,000 attending outpatient departments, 2,580 pregnant and lactating women, 2,500 children under the age of five for immunization, and 15,200 for health promotion activities. Additionally, capacity building for all staff members and Community Health Workers (CHWs) in the first quarter of the project. The services offered will include basic primary healthcare, emergency trauma care, referral for complex cases, and intensified prevention activities such as health education and hygiene promotion.ltbrgtThe project will establish three fixed health facilities, comprising one health center and one Primary Health Unit (PHU). The health center is in Sigalow, while the PHU will be set up in Qoydo. These fixed facilities will serve both host communities and internally displaced persons (IDPs) residing in underserved and hard-to-reach areas. The health center will operate 24 hours a day, offering comprehensive healthcare services.ltbrgtThe Primary Health Unit in Qoydo will primarily provide outpatient consultations, immunization services, emergency care, as well as health communication and risk mitigation activities.ltbrgtIn addition, a mobile health team will be stationed in Dharkenley, which will serve as its logistical hub. The mobile team will serve high-reach areas where there is an access constraint. The team will work for 6 days and will serve 6 villages ( Dharkenley, Lugbari, Haradey, Bacadbuko, Dhayga reer wabar and Horjoog with approx. population of 15 thousand people and mobile clinic will be serving one day per village. These are villages in which Hidig has assessed and have seen the health gap and community willingness to collaborate with humanitarian partners.ltbrgtThe team will deliver essential health services to clusters of remote villages that are geographically isolated from Baletweyne town. Services provided by the mobile team will include outpatient consultations, immunizations, antenatal and post-natal care (ANC/PNC), community engagement activities, and emergency referral services.ltbrgtMoreover, the project will integrate protection, GBV, and mental health services, ensuring appropriate referrals to higher levels of care. Simultaneously, it will enhance the capacity of health facility committees and community-level health service provision in the targeted area, with inclusive representation from key community stakeholders, including people living with disabilities. Furthermore, the project will be coordinated with other sectors such as WASH, Nutrition, food security and livelihood, which also focus on this location, providing a comprehensive assistance package to the targeted beneficiaries. The project team will ensure that they closely coordinate as well with any other existing operational partners in these locations to avoid duplication and ensure complementarity. HIDIG will also attend cluster meetings, mainly Health, Nutrition, WASH and food security taking place in the state and the region.ltbrgtlt/pgt
